result: TARDIS is a novel two-step transgenesis approach that splits library introduction from genomic integration, enabling transformation of a single individual to yield thousands of genetically unique transgenic individuals through heritable TARDIS library arrays and engineered landing pads, representing a 1000-fold increase in throughput over traditional methods.
evaluation: All three reviewers affirm the novelty and effectiveness of the TARDIS approach. Reviewer 1 states 'the data for the effectiveness of the method is solid,' Reviewer 2 notes the authors 'demonstrate two possible applications of the technology' with 'many important controls, showcasing the potential of the method,' and Reviewer 3 describes 'the clever design of the selection markers' and confirms the work 'provides a protocol for doing so and tool to make it practical.'

result: Large, heritable barcode libraries containing thousands of unique sequences (up to ~800,000 in injection mix, 1,319-3,001 unique barcodes per array) can be created and maintained as extrachromosomal arrays in C. elegans using randomized synthesized oligos via complexing PCR with minimal jackpotting.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'The conclusions for applications of this method in C. elegans are supported by the data' and notes the authors 'demonstrate two possible applications of the technology: individually barcoded lineages for lineage tracing.' Reviewer 1 confirms 'the data for the effectiveness of the method is solid.' No reviewer challenges the barcode library generation data.

result: Individual barcode sequences are selected and integrated from TARDIS arrays upon Cas9 induction with frequencies strongly correlated (R ≈ 0.96) to their prevalence in the array, with approximately 200-300 worms needed to obtain an integrated line, and integration events can be validated by hygromycin selection and sequencing.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 states 'The conclusions for applications of this method in C. elegans are supported by the data' and describes the work as including 'many important controls.' Reviewer 3 notes the use of 'selection markers to identify successful events of integration' as a strength. The correlation data and integration efficiency are not questioned by any reviewer.

result: TARDIS is compatible with integration of large promoters (330 bp to 5.5 kb) and can simultaneously integrate promoters into multiple genomic locations using dual landing pad sites, with transcriptional reporters for nine genes recovered from a single heat shock of a single TARDIS array line containing 13 promoters.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly confirms 'The conclusions for applications of this method in C. elegans are supported by the data' and notes the authors demonstrate 'transcriptional reporter lines generated by inserting multiple promoters' as one of two applications. Reviewer 3 describes the 'distinct strategies of selection to...Introduce promoters at two specific genomic landing pads downstream of fluorescent reporters' as a strength of the study.

result: A novel split-selection hygromycin resistance landing pad was designed that requires perfect integration on both the 5' and 3' ends of a synthetic intron for functional resistance, providing dual-sided selection to minimize incomplete integrations compared to previous single-sided selection systems.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly identifies 'the clever design of the selection markers, which enrich the collection of this type of markers' as a strength of the study. Reviewer 2 describes the landing pad design as part of the 'general approach' that is well-demonstrated. No reviewer challenges the landing pad design or its effectiveness.

result: During array formation, a subset of barcode sequences unexpectedly increase in frequency (jackpotting) independent of injection mix composition, with arrays ranging considerably in diversity and following Poisson distributions; the authors propose this reflects array size effects on maintenance rather than fragment size bias.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 states 'the authors discuss important observations and considerations' regarding the method, which would include the array formation observations. No reviewer challenges the jackpotting observations or the proposed mechanistic explanations. The data on array diversity and frequency distributions are accepted as part of the overall supported findings.

result: TARDIS integration is highly efficient with transgenic individuals readily detected, co-conversion occurs at high rates (~50%) when targeting multiple sites simultaneously, and while split-selection allows direct verification, sequencing confirmation is recommended as errors including internal deletions can occur (5/83 incorrect sequences observed).
evaluation: Reviewer 1 states 'the data for the effectiveness of the method is solid,' which encompasses the integration efficiency findings. Reviewer 2 notes the work includes 'many important controls' and that conclusions are 'supported by the data.' The observation of some incorrect integrations and the recommendation for sequencing confirmation are presented as practical considerations rather than fundamental flaws.

result: For all promoters tested, expression was seen in at least one previously reported tissue but was absent in one or more tissues for several promoters, with fluorophore expression concentrated in but not exclusive to the nucleus; differences from previously reported patterns may reflect promoter region differences or the single developmental stage examined.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 states 'The conclusions for applications of this method in C. elegans are supported by the data' which includes the promoter expression characterization. The expression pattern observations and potential explanations for differences are presented as descriptive findings that are not challenged by any reviewer.

result: TARDIS increases transformation yields up to approximately 1000-fold over current single-step methods, providing an approximately 1000×-fold increase in barcoding throughput in C. elegans and making it a unique resource among multicellular models.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 affirms 'the data for the effectiveness of the method is solid' and notes this is 'a valuable contribution.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'The conclusions for applications of this method in C. elegans are supported by the data.' The 1000-fold increase claim is central to the paper's significance and is not questioned by any reviewer.

result: The TARDIS process is conceptually adaptable to any system where experimentally generated genomic landing pads and diverse, heritable DNA elements can be generated, though adaptation to systems beyond C. elegans would require methods to introduce large heritable libraries into the germline as most systems do not maintain extrachromosomal arrays.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly notes 'the potential application of the method beyond C. elegans...remains speculative at this point given that a nontrivial aspect of the success of the method in worms is the self-assembly of DNA into heritable extrachromosomal arrays (a feature that is absent in most other systems).' This indicates the reviewers recognize the claims about broader applicability as speculative rather than demonstrated.

result: TARDIS provides the first true library-based approach for multiplexing transgenesis in C. elegans, as prior multiplexed methods (library mosSCI, RMCE, guide pool arrays, and recent work by Mouridi et al.) have not demonstrated multiplexing beyond tens of unique sequences—orders of magnitude below what is needed for exploratory transgenesis.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 acknowledges 'the work is not methodologically novel - it adds to other recent studies, e.g. from Nonet, Mouridi et al., and Malaiwong et al, that use the integration of single and multiple/diverse DNA sequences in the C. elegans genome' but confirms it 'provides a protocol for doing so and tool to make it practical.' Reviewer 1 notes 'The advantages of this approach in terms of ease and effectiveness relative to others with similar aims will emerge as they are put to more general use.' The comparison to prior methods is accepted as context.

result: Not all arrays contained all 13 injected plasmids despite arrays being large enough (1-13 MB) to hold all plasmids; this differential presence was somewhat unexpected and may reflect preferential use of linear fragments in array assembly, suggesting future use of linear fragments may increase incorporation and diversity.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 notes 'the authors discuss important observations and considerations' which includes these observations about array composition. The finding is presented as an unexpected observation with a speculative explanation, and no reviewer challenges the data or interpretation. This is treated as a practical consideration for future optimization.
